newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: South African stock market closing report.

text.p: Spending much of the day languishing around fairly firm levels attained in the morning, South African industrial shares pushed up in afternoon trade, driven by futures players and strong institutional interest.
The industrial index ended what dealers called a "hectic" day nearly one percent higher.
"It was slow to start but the ball soon gathered momentum. It was pretty hectic in later trade. There were some big trades going through," one dealer said.
Dealers said lines of select stocks were traded and that this hinted at institutional activity.
They added that trade was characterised by such institutional interest as well as by busy futures trade which saw futures players buy stocks and sell the underlying futures.
"There were select lines done so the institutions must have been in. That's usually the way it happens," a dealer said.
Morning trade was fairly hushed in typical pre-Christmas lethargy but activity picked up substantially later.
"Most of the guys are absent. They've already started their Christmas holidays," a dealer said.
Technical and mining and exploration stocks featured.
Gold shares struggled higher throguhoiut the day after starting on a dip below open, weighed by listless bullion.
Still they closed a tad better.
Industrials rose 77 points to 7,897.4, all-shares were up 51.2 points at 6,666.4 and golds added 8.6 points to 1,526.4.
Remgro was up 105 cents to 42.90 rand, Loraine was down 40 cents to 13.30 rand, Gold Fields put on 300 cents to 139 rand, Engen was up 70 cents to 25 rand and Sasol rose 100 cents to 57.25 rand.
Industrial and all-share equity futures contracts bounced in early trade on the back of Wall Street's overnight rebound.
Those contracts continued climbing throughout the day, despite market talk earlier that they would be pressured by institusional selling.
Gold futures also braved a climb and ended firmer than settlement levels.
The December industrial contract was much firmer at 7,636/45 from 7,490, the all share was carried to 6,100/30 from 5,996 and the all gold was at 1,062/67 from 1,053.
